_readme: Tuned config for orange/brownish ARPES flake detection on SiO2/Si substrate.
Calibrated from 17 good + 15 bad sample images.
Detection strategy: flakes are found by substrate-border exclusion (not color-first),
so whole flakes are detected even when they have internal color gradients.
Each candidate is then scored by how much of it is the target orange color —
green blobs and grid markers (color_fraction near 0) are dropped at that stage.
closing_kernel_size=0: closing is intentionally disabled on the substrate mask.
Closing would merge nearby differently-colored objects (orange flake + green debris)
into a single mixed-color candidate, corrupting the color_fraction filter.
The isolation score counts ALL non-substrate debris (including green/teal).

marker_rgb_range._comment: Bright pink/magenta location markers. R ~255, G ~197, B ~255.

_comment: H in degrees [0-360], S/V in percent [0-100] -- the common color-picker scale
(e.g. Windows Paint), converted to OpenCV's own scale internally -- never enter
H 210-290 covers blue through blue-purple hues.
V 7.8-60.8 captures the medium-dark substrate without catching bright flakes.
Widen V_max if substrate appears brighter in your images.
Target color: orange/brownish flakes on the chip.
H in degrees [0-360], S/V in percent [0-100] -- the common color-picker scale
(e.g. Windows Paint), converted to OpenCV's own scale internally -- never enter
H 6-56 covers the full orange range observed (5th-95th pct across all samples).
S 11.8-51.0 targets moderately saturated orange; excludes pale pink grid markers.
V 51.0-86.3 avoids the dark substrate and blown-out reflections.
